- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for consecutive positive sentiment.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.0) — increase forecast by 2–5% for consecutive negative sentiment.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak of recent 3-day high.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lag in downward corrections — if true price drops >5% from recent peak, forecast should adjust 1–2 days earlier than observed.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts overestimate early in trend (first 5–7 days) — apply 3–5% downward bias to first 7 days of forecast.
- Sentiment reversal triggers correction — if sentiment shifts from + to - or vice versa, adjust forecast midpoint by -10% to +10% depending on direction.
